title: Quantum Machine Learning
tagline: Learn qubits, gates, and circuits, then train variational circuits, quantum classifiers, and quantum kernels, and see where the limits are.
prereqs: Machine Learning and Python & Math for AI (vectors, matrices, complex numbers help). No physics background needed.

steps.title: How quantum computers compute
steps.why: A visual tour of the math behind qubits and quantum gates.

steps.title: Qubits and superposition
steps.why: What a qubit state is and what measuring it gives you.

steps.title: Entanglement
steps.why: Correlated qubits that can't be described one at a time.

steps.title: Quantum gates
steps.why: The basic gates that rotate and combine qubit states.

steps.title: Quantum circuits
steps.why: IBM lesson on reading and composing circuits of gates and measurements.

steps.title: A quantum algorithm: Grover's search
steps.why: 3Blue1Brown walks through Grover's search and its square-root speedup.

steps.title: What quantum advantage means
steps.why: Which problems might gain from quantum hardware, and which won't.

steps.title: What quantum machine learning is
steps.why: Computerphile overview of mixing quantum circuits with machine learning.

steps.title: Encoding classical data into qubits
steps.why: Basis, angle, and amplitude ways to load data into a circuit.

steps.title: Variational quantum circuits
steps.why: Circuits with trainable angles, optimized by a classical computer.

steps.title: Build a quantum classifier
steps.why: Qiskit summer school lecture: encode data, train a circuit, classify.

steps.title: Quantum kernels and SVMs
steps.why: Use a circuit as a feature map, then train a classical SVM on it.

steps.title: Variational quantum eigensolver
steps.why: Find a molecule's ground-state energy with a trainable circuit in PennyLane.

steps.title: Barren plateaus
steps.why: Why gradients of large random circuits vanish, and ways to avoid it.

projects: Build and simulate Bell-state and Grover circuits in Qiskit, and plot the measurement counts.
Train a 2-qubit variational classifier in PennyLane on a small 2D dataset and compare it with logistic regression.
Compare a quantum-kernel SVM with an RBF-kernel SVM on the same dataset and write up accuracy and runtime.
